title: Brittle Fracture
quiz_topic: Brittle Fracture and Vessel Thermal Stress

objectives.text: Without references, EXPLAIN the importance of controlling heatup and cooldown rates of the primary coolant system.

passages.quote: Ductile fracture is exhibited when metals can sustain substantial plastic strain or deformation before fracturing.
Brittle fracture is exhibited when metals fracture with a relatively small or negligible amount of plastic strain.

Ductile fracture is better than brittle fracture, because ductile fracture occurs over a period of time, where as brittle fracture is fast, and can occur (with flaws) at lower stress levels than a ductile fracture.
Nil-Ductility Transition (NDT) temperature is the temperature above which a material is ductile and below which it is brittle.
Small grain size tends to increase ductility and results in a decrease in NDT temperature.
The NDT temperature can also be lowered by small additions of selected alloying elements such as nickel and manganese to low-carbon steels.
Consequently, during operation the reactor vessel is subjected to an increasing fluence (flux) of fast neutrons, and as a result the NDT temperature increases steadily.

One of the biggest concerns with brittle fracture is that it can occur at stresses well below the yield strength (stress corresponding to the transition from elastic to plastic behavior) of the material, provided certain conditions are present.
The temperature at which the yield and tensile strength coincide is the NDT temperature.
Therefore, if a flaw exists, any failure at a temperature equal or below the NDT temperature for flawed material will be brittle.
It should be noted that smaller grain size, higher temperature, and lower stress tend to mitigate crack initiation.
Larger grain size, lower temperatures, and higher stress tend to favor crack propagation.
There is a stress level below which a crack will not propagate at any temperature.
the crack will initiate and propagate through the material at great speeds (speed of sound).
Fracture toughness is an indication of the amount of stress required to propagate a preexisting flaw.
The intersection of the crack arrest curve with the yield curve (Curve B) is called the fracture transition elastic (FTE) point.
The temperature corresponding with this point is normally about 120°F above the NDT temperature.
Above this temperature, only ductile fractures occur.
For greater safety, it is desirable that operation be limited above the FTE temperature, or NDT + 60°F.
Minimum pressurization-temperature (MPT) curves specify the temperature and pressure limitations for reactor plant operation.
They are based on reactor vessel and head stress limitations and the need to preclude reactor vessel and head brittle fracture.
Note that the safe operating region is to the right of the reactor vessel MPT curve.
MPT curve will shift to the right due to irradiation.
The precaution to be observed when performing a hydrostatic test is to make sure the pressure is consistent with plant temperatures.
Heatup and cooldown rate limits are based upon impact on the future fatigue life of the plant.
The heatup and cooldown rate limits ensure that the plant's fatigue life is equal to or greater than the plant's operational life.
Large components such as flanges, reactor vessel head, and the vessel itself are the limiting components.
Usually exceeding the heatup or cooldown rate limits requires only an assessment of the impact on the future fatigue life of the plant.
Soak times are used so that heating can be carefully controlled.
Become very significant if system is at room temperature or below and very close to RTNDT temperature limitations

body.text: In brittle fracture, cracks propagate rapidly, and failure results from cleavage, or splitting along definite planes.

checks.q: Why is ductile fracture better than brittle fracture?
o: It occurs only at low temperature
It occurs over a period of time, while brittle fracture is fast
It occurs at lower stress
It leaves no cracks
checks.x: Ductile fracture occurs over a period of time, whereas brittle fracture is fast and can occur, with flaws, at lower stress levels.

o: Fracture with a relatively small or negligible amount of plastic strain
Fracture after substantial plastic strain
Slow cracking under constant load
Failure by general corrosion
checks.x: Brittle fracture is exhibited when metals fracture with a relatively small or negligible amount of plastic strain.

body.text: Many steels are ductile at elevated temperatures and brittle at low temperatures.
NDT is not precise. It varies with prior mechanical and heat treatment and with the nature and amounts of impurity elements, and is found by a drop-weight test such as the Izod or Charpy test.
Grain size is controlled by heat treatment in the specifications and manufacturing of reactor vessels.
The reactor vessel is continuously exposed to fast neutrons that escape from the core.
During shutdown or an abnormal cooldown, the temperature may fall below the NDT value while the internal pressure is still high, and the vessel is then susceptible to brittle fracture.

checks.q: What two changes are made to reactor pressure vessels to decrease NDT?
o: Smaller grain size and small additions of alloying elements such as nickel and manganese
Larger grain size and more carbon
Thicker walls and higher pressure
Cladding and cold working
checks.x: Changes made to decrease NDT include use of smaller grain size and small additions of selected alloying elements such as nickel and manganese to low-carbon steels.

checks.q: What happens to the NDT temperature of a reactor vessel during operation?
o: It decreases steadily
It stays the same
It cycles up and down with power
It increases steadily
checks.x: The vessel is subjected to an increasing fluence of fast neutrons, and as a result the NDT temperature increases steadily.

items: A flaw such as a crack
Stress sufficient to develop a small deformation at the crack tip

body.cap: Stress-Temperature Diagram for Crack Initiation and Arrest
body.alt: Stress against temperature: tensile strength curve A, yield strength curve B, tensile strength with flaw curve C, and crack arrest curve D. NDT with no flaw is at 10°F, NDT with a small flaw at 60°F, FTE at 70°F, and FTP where curves A and D meet.

body.text: As temperature goes down, tensile strength (Curve A) and yield strength (Curve B) increase. At some low temperature, on the order of 10°F for carbon steel, they coincide.

When a small flaw is present, tensile strength follows dashed Curve C. About 50°F above the no-flaw NDT temperature, it drops to the yield curve, and where Curves C and B meet there is a new NDT temperature.

checks.q: Which is one of the three conditions necessary for brittle fracture?
o: A flaw such as a crack
A temperature well above NDT
A low stress level with no flaws
A small grain size
checks.x: Brittle fracture requires a flaw such as a crack, stress sufficient to develop a small deformation at the crack tip, and a temperature at or below NDT.

checks.q: On a stress-temperature diagram, where is the NDT temperature with no flaw?
o: Where the crack arrest curve meets the yield curve
Where the crack arrest curve meets the tensile curve
At the lower fracture propagation stress
Where the yield and tensile strength coincide
checks.x: The temperature at which the yield and tensile strength coincide is the NDT temperature.

body.text: Brittle failure generally occurs because a flaw or crack propagates through the material. If a plastic flaw exists at the tip, the metal around the crack supports the stress and the structure is not endangered.
When brittle fracture occurs,
This stress level is called the lower fracture propagation stress. As temperature increases, a higher stress is needed for a crack to propagate. That relationship is the crack arrest curve, Curve D.

items: Extent of deformations to the crystal structure

checks.q: Which conditions tend to mitigate crack initiation?
o: Larger grain size, lower temperature, and higher stress
Smaller grain size, lower temperature, and higher stress
Larger grain size, higher temperature, and lower stress
Smaller grain size, higher temperature, and lower stress
checks.x: Smaller grain size, higher temperature, and lower stress tend to mitigate crack initiation.

checks.q: Which is one of the five factors that determine fracture toughness?
o: Reactor power
Metal grain size
Vessel diameter
Coolant flow rate
checks.x: The factors are metal composition, metal temperature, extent of deformations to the crystal structure, metal grain size, and metal crystalline form.

o: An indication of the amount of stress required to propagate a preexisting flaw
The temperature at which a metal becomes brittle
The work to deform a cubic inch of metal
The hardness of a metal
checks.x: Fracture toughness is an indication of the amount of stress required to propagate a preexisting flaw.

body.text: The FTE temperature is normally about 60°F above the NDT temperature, and is also known as the Reference Temperature - Nil-ductility Transition (RTNDT). It is the temperature above which plastic deformation accompanies all fractures.
The intersection of the crack arrest curve (Curve D) and the tensile strength curve (Curve A) is the fracture transition plastic (FTP) point.

body.alt: Stress against temperature relative to NDT, with fracture initiation curves for 1, 8, 12, and 24 inch flaws, the crack arrest curve, FTE, and FTP.

body.text: Operation must be above the NDT temperature to be certain that no brittle fracture can occur.
Under those conditions, no brittle fracture can occur for purely elastic loads.

checks.q: Where is the fracture transition elastic (FTE) point on a stress-temperature diagram?
o: Where Curve C meets Curve B
Where the crack arrest curve meets the yield curve
Where the crack arrest curve meets the tensile strength curve
Where yield and tensile strength coincide
checks.x: The intersection of the crack arrest curve with the yield curve (Curve B) is called the fracture transition elastic (FTE) point.

checks.q: About how far above NDT is the fracture transition plastic (FTP) temperature?
checks.x: The FTP temperature is normally about 120°F above the NDT temperature.

body.text: The curve ensures adequate operating margin away from the crack arrest curve. Curves used by operations also include instrument error.
This shift accounts for the increased brittleness or decreased ductility from neutron irradiation.

checks.q: What are minimum pressurization-temperature curves based on?
o: Pump seal limits and tank level
Neutron flux and control rod worth
Reactor vessel and head stress limitations and preventing vessel and head brittle fracture
Fuel temperature limits and coolant flow
checks.x: They are based on reactor vessel and head stress limitations and the need to preclude reactor vessel and head brittle fracture.

checks.q: Where is the safe operating region on an MPT curve?
o: To the left of the curve
Above the curve
Exactly on the curve
To the right of the curve
checks.x: The safe operating region is to the right of the reactor vessel MPT curve.

checks.q: What is the precaution for hydrostatic testing?
o: Make sure the pressure is consistent with plant temperatures
Make sure the test is at the lowest temperature
Make sure the reactor is critical
Make sure the relief valves are removed
checks.x: The precaution is to make sure the pressure is consistent with plant temperatures.

body.text: Usually the most limiting component sets the heatup and cooldown rates.
This may depend on the individual plant and its limiting components.

checks.q: Which components set the limits on heatup and cooldown rates?
o: Large components such as flanges, the vessel head, and the vessel
Small instrument lines
Fuel assemblies
Electrical cables
checks.x: Large components such as flanges, reactor vessel head, and the vessel itself are the limiting components.

checks.q: What is typically required when a heatup or cooldown rate limit is exceeded?
o: An immediate reactor scram
Replacement of the vessel head
A hydrostatic test
Only an assessment of the impact on future fatigue life
checks.x: Usually exceeding the heatup or cooldown rate limits requires only an assessment of the impact on the future fatigue life of the plant.

body.text: Soak times may be required during heatup, especially when large limiting components are involved.

This minimizes thermal stresses. For example, the coolant is heated to a specified temperature and held there for a set time, so the metal in a large component heats more evenly from the hot side to the cold side.

o: To test the relief valves
To minimize thermal stresses by carefully controlling heating
To reduce neutron flux
To remove oxygen from the coolant
checks.x: Soak times are used so that heating can be carefully controlled, minimizing thermal stresses.

checks.q: When do soak times become very significant?
o: At room temperature or below and very close to RTNDT limitations
At full power
Just before a scram
At maximum system temperature
checks.x: Soak times become very significant if the system is at room temperature or below and very close to RTNDT temperature limitations.

examples.title: Find the temperature after an NDT shift
examples.problem: The FTE was 60°F at the beginning of vessel life, and the NDT changed by 300°F over time. What temperature must the coolant be above before full system pressure can be applied?
steps: Irradiation raises the NDT, and the FTE moves with it.
Add the shift to the starting FTE: 60°F + 300°F.

facts.a: Fracture of a metal that can sustain substantial plastic strain or deformation before fracturing.

facts.q: What three conditions tend to mitigate crack initiation?
facts.a: Smaller grain size, higher temperature, and lower stress.

facts.q: What five factors determine the fracture toughness of a metal?
facts.a: Metal composition, metal temperature, extent of deformations to the crystal structure, metal grain size, and metal crystalline form.

facts.q: How far above NDT are the FTE and FTP temperatures?
facts.a: FTE is normally about 60°F above NDT, and FTP about 120°F above NDT.

facts.q: Where is the safe operating region on an MPT curve?
facts.a: To the right of the curve.
So heating can be carefully controlled, which minimizes thermal stresses.

summary.text: Ductile fracture follows substantial plastic strain, and brittle fracture follows a small or negligible amount.
NDT decreases due to smaller grain size and increases due to irradiation.
Brittle fracture requires a flaw such as a crack, stress sufficient to develop a small deformation at the crack tip, and a temperature at or below NDT.
MPT curves are based on reactor vessel and head stress limitations, and the safe operating region is to the right of the curve.
Heatup and cooldown rate limits are based upon impact on the future fatigue life of the plant.
Soak times are used to minimize thermal stresses by controlling the heating rate.
